items.title: [Server] Stop the stdio server from answering a notification it refuses
items.excerpt: A notification sent before `initialize` got a `-32600` back over stdio, but a notification must never be answered ([basic](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#notifications)). Over HTTP the refusal keeps its `400`, which the spec allows - stdio has no status to carry it, so it's only logged now. [P08]

items.title: [Server] Refuse a 2026-07-28 request with a null id instead of dropping it
items.excerpt: `StatelessProtocol` took `"id": null` for a notification and acknowledged it, so the client never got an answer. MCP forbids a null id on requests ([basic](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#requests)) and JSON-RPC only treats a missing `id` as a notification - it's refused with `-32600` now, like the handshake era already does. [P05]

Both are refused with `-32600` now ([basic](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic#messages)). [P04]

items.title: fix: reject integer parameters at or above 2^63
items.excerpt: ## Summary Integer parameter parsing now rejects values at or above 2^63. Before, they slipped past the range check and came out as `MinInt` (amd64) or `MaxInt` (arm64). ## Why `math.MaxInt64` can't be represented as a float64 and rounds up to 2^63, so `f > math.MaxInt` lets 2^63 through. That includes `"9223372036854775807"`. Go doesn't define the result of converting an out-of-range float to an int. Fixes #3489 ##

This preserves ordering, duplicates, and the treatment of non-string or empty values. A unit test covers mixed claim values and duplicates. items.title: [Server] Fix `"0"` prefix offering all completions
items.excerpt: `empty("0")` is true, so `EnumCompletionProvider` and `ListCompletionProvider` returned every value for the prefix `0` instead of only the ones starting with it. Now only an empty prefix offers everything. Spotted while reviewing #652, which pinned the behavior in a test - replaced here. #649 adds the same test for the list provider and needs an update after this.

items.title: [Tests] Stop php -S servers together with their forked workers
items.excerpt: Stopping a `php -S` process only ended the master, so its `PHP_CLI_SERVER_WORKERS` were reparented and kept the port and the inherited stdout/stderr open, which made `make integration-tests | tail` hang after the suite finished. Every test that starts a `php -S` server now stops it through `ServerProcess::stop()`, which ends the whole process tree.

When a request's fiber is dropped while it waits for the server, e.g. a `2026-07-28` handler asked the client for input and the `input_required` answer ended the request, and the handler throws while it unwinds (in a `finally`), `HandlerFiberState::threw()` kept the throwable for a rethrow that never comes: the failure was lost without a trace. `HandlerFibers::step()` now marks the state while the

items.title: [Server] Read only new entries when polling `InMemoryNotificationBus`
items.excerpt: `InMemoryNotificationBus::since()` walked its whole backlog on every poll, so each caught-up `subscriptions/listen` stream paid for every entry kept. Sequences have no gaps, so it now reads from the cursor only, and hands the backlog back in one go to a reader that fell behind it. On PHP 8.5, a caught-up poll drops from 2.9 µs to 0.07 µs with the default backlog of 256, and from 114 µs to 0.07 µs with 10,000 entries.

items.title: [Server] Fix variadic enum parameters declaring their items as objects

The items now list the enum's values, like for a single enum parameter, so the call validates and the handler gets the enum cases. Found, fixed and written up with Claude Code.

items.title: [Server] Fix iterable parameters being declared as objects
items.excerpt: An `iterable $items` parameter was advertised as `{"type": "object"}`, so `{"items": [1, 2]}` got `-32602 Expected object, but received array`, although `iterable ` already maps to `array` and the argument is cast like an `array` one. It now gets `{"type": "array"}`, which means a JSON object is refused instead, as for `array`, hence the `[BC Break]` entry. Found, fixed and written up with Claude Code.
